tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kit Surfaces
tips.text: Use Tamiya PlastiKote Thinner or Mr. Hobby Paint Thinner to dissolve old acrylics. Apply with a soft brush, let sit 5 minutes, then gently wipe with a cloth. For stubborn spots, use a cotton swab dipped in acetone (avoiding Tamiya plastic cement). Test on a small area first. After cleaning, apply a light coat of Tamiya Clear Primer to seal the surface and prevent further paint migration. Always work in a well-ventilated area.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: For bent or broken photo-etch (PE) parts, use a hobby knife and sanding stick to carefully bend or reshape. If a part is broken, use Eduard PE Repair Putty or Microscale PE Glue. Apply a thin layer, press into place, and let dry. For fine details, use a dental pick to adjust. Avoid overfilling to maintain the PE's delicate structure. Sand lightly after drying with 1000-grit wet sandpaper.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an Iwata airbrush, disassemble and soak the nozzle in Tamiya Acrylic Thinner for 10 minutes. Use a syringe to flush the nozzle with thin wash. For stubborn clogs, use a 1:1 mix of Tami, Vallejo, and AK Interactive water-based thinners. If the tip is damaged, replace it with a new Iwata tip. Always clean the airbrush after each use with a dedicated airbrush cleaner to prevent future clogs.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: Frost forms on rattle cans due to condensation. To prevent this, store cans in a cool, dry place and use them at room temperature. Before spraying, warm the can in a water bath (not exceeding 40°C). Use a Tamiya Rattle Can Heated Adapter for consistent temperature. Avoid shaking the can; instead, gently roll it to mix. Apply thin coats to minimize condensation buildup.

tips.title: Fixing Paint Reactions and Bubbling
tips.text: Paint reactions (bubbling, wrinkling) often result from applying too thick a coat. Use a Tamiya 1:10 water-thinner mix for acrylics or a 1:1 mix of Vallejo and AK Interactive water-based thinners. Apply with an airbrush at 10-15 psi. For existing bubbles, sand gently with 1000-grit sandpaper, apply a thin primer, and repaint. Use a wet brush for precise areas. Always test paint consistency on a scrap panel before applying to the model.
